errors.meaning: The acting user is not Accounts.

planningRules.rule: Say what a round does not do. It collects what people ask for; it buys nothing, approves nothing and moves no money (BR-9, AC-1 of the approval that follows is a separate act).
Say that the low items are offered, not added. Every requester sees what the store already knows is short and chooses whether to include it — nothing joins a request on their behalf (BR-3, A2, AC-2).
Never collect the requests yourself. Each member of staff submits their own, and one person typing everybody's list is the thing the round exists to replace (BR-8).
Say that an urgent request does not need the round. Something needed at once is raised outside one and accepted just the same, so a round closing is not a deadline on need (BR-1, A1, E4).

planningRules.rule: Never write the reason. It is what the approver reads before deciding to spend the school's money, and a reason a planner supplied is a justification nobody gave (BR-5, E3, AC-3).
Never round or invent a quantity. It goes into the item's own unit, and a request for "some paper" is a number nobody can buy against (BR-4, E1, E2).

Check the unit before the number. Ten of an item counted in reams and ten counted in boxes are different orders, and the requester rarely says which they meant (BR-4, and the item's unit is fixed at UC-18-01 BR-2).

Say what was offered and left out. Items already below their reorder level are put in front of every requester, and the one thing the store has actually run out of is the easiest to leave off a list of what one classroom wants (BR-3, A2, AC-2).

Never say the goods are on the way. Submitting buys nothing: the request has to be approved by whichever role its value requires, then cash has to be released by a different role, then somebody has to go and buy it (BR-9).
Never treat a missing round as a refusal. A request outside a round is accepted as urgent, which is the point — a lab out of a reagent cannot wait for the end of the period (BR-1, A1, E4).

fields.name: by_item
fields.description: The round grouped by item, with the total quantity asked for across every requester. Whether the same item is bought once against the round or once per requester is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2).

fields.name: awaiting_decision
fields.description: Requests submitted and not yet approved or rejected. Nothing has been bought for any of them (BR-9).

fields.name: advanced_not_received
fields.description: Requests where cash has been issued and the goods have not arrived. This is money out of the school with nothing to show for it yet (UC-18-03 BR-6).

fields.name: rejected_by_requester
fields.description: Rejections grouped by who asked. A member of staff whose requests are always rejected is visible only because nothing is ever deleted (BR-11).

fields.name: estimated_value_source
fields.description: Unknown. The figure decides which role must approve, and nothing in the system holds a price for a stock item (OQ-3).

errors.meaning: The actor is asking about requests that are not theirs.
errors.note: A requester sees their own and the round page is the School Admin's and the Principal's (BR-6, BR-7). The use case writes no exception for a request outside that.

planningRules.rule: Answer "where does my request stand" with the stage and what it means. Approved is not bought, advanced is cash out with nothing received, and received is not settled — the states read like progress and only two of them mean the goods exist (BR-7).
Group the round by item when the question is about the round. A round read one request at a time cannot be bought for in one order, which is the whole reason every request gathers on one page (BR-6).
Name the requests that have cash out and no goods in. That is the module's real exposure, and it is invisible in a list sorted by requester (BR-9).
Never present the estimated value as a price. Nothing in the system holds one for a stock item, and this figure is what decides which role must approve the spend (OQ-3).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: meri request ka kya bana?
request.gloss: what happened to my request?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Say which stage it is at and what that actually means — approved is a decision to spend, not goods on a shelf; advanced means somebody has the cash and has not come back yet. Where it was rejected, give the reason as it was written, since that is the whole point of the reason being required.

request.text: is round mein kis ne kya manga hai?
request.gloss: who has asked for what this round?

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, round closed with 14 requests.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Give it grouped by item with the total quantity across everybody, not request by request — that is what can be bought in one order. Say that whether the same item is bought once for the round or once per requester is not settled anywhere, and that the estimated values shown come from nothing the system holds.
